title: Optimal Transistor Folding and Placement for Synthesizing Standard Cells of Complementary FET Technology
problem: CFET-based standard cell synthesis requires optimally determining transistor folding shapes and placement order while guaranteeing vertical routing space on stacked FETs and accommodating buried power rails, which significantly impact cell area and routability.
motivation: As VLSI scales beyond 5nm, standard cells must shrink further, and CFET's vertical stacking offers area benefits but introduces new optimization challenges not present in conventional FET designs.
method: Proposes a search tree-based area-optimal method combining transistor folding and placement decisions. Accelerates cost computation using dynamic programming for partial solutions and ensures routing feasibility by formulating vertical space verification as a network flow problem.
key_novelty: Joint optimization of transistor folding shapes and placement order via search tree with dynamic programming acceleration and network flow-based routing feasibility verification.
contributions: Search tree-based method for optimal combined transistor folding and placement in CFET standard cells
Dynamic programming formulation for accelerating cost computation of partial solutions
Network flow formulation for verifying vertical routing space feasibility on stacked FETs
CFET cell synthesizer achieving 5% area reduction, 38% shorter metal length, and 70% less metal2 usage versus state-of-the-art

metrics.other: 38% shorter total metal length, 70% less metal2 for in-cell routing

limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract.
